stem.en: Kabir suggests the blocked cell "could just stop swallowing, then it would not shrink". What would that save, and what would it not?

text.en: It would save the wall. It would not save the products stuck inside, or the silence: nothing made for outside can leave, and a nerve still cannot signal.

feedback.en: Balance of wall, yes. The exit is still blocked, so nothing the cell makes can get out.

text.en: It would make things worse, because the cell would starve.

feedback.en: Most cells get sugar through carriers, not by swallowing. Stopping swallowing is survivable. Stopping spitting is not.

text.en: The cell cannot choose to stop swallowing.

feedback.en: Cells do regulate it. The point is that regulating the in-leg cannot fix a blocked out-leg.

explanation.en: Two failures had one cause: the blocked exit. Fixing the wall budget fixes one symptom and leaves the disease.
